plain.text: Sarah lived to be 127 years old and died at Hebron in Canaan. Abraham mourned and wept for her. He then spoke to the Hittites living there: "I am a foreigner and stranger among you. Sell me some property for a burial site." They honoured him and offered him the best of their tombs. Abraham asked to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron. Ephron offered to give it to him, but Abraham insisted on paying the full price. Ephron named it: four hundred shekels of silver. Abraham weighed out the silver in front of everyone, and the field and cave became his property. He buried Sarah there. It was the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned.

summary.bigIdea: Abraham grieves for Sarah and buys a burial place, his first piece of the promised land.
points: Sarah dies, and Abraham mourns and weeps for her.
Abraham carefully and honestly buys a field and cave for her burial.
This grave is the first part of Canaan that belongs to Abraham's family.
summary.reflection: Abraham wept for Sarah. How do you think faith and grief can belong together?
